title: Meera's infra hotlist + shift notes
content:
Quick log / brain dump for today's shift - rapid bits, not polished.

03/12 08:15 — startup
- coffee. salted caramel.
- quick health scan: 3 racks show elevated temp in north datacenter (rack A12, A13, A14) — flagged to SRE Slack #dc-alarms.
- autoscaler alert at 07:58: spike on hosted-api (p50 latency jumped from 42 -> 110ms for 512-token jobs). looked like burst from a small customer running long sequences.

Top priorities (start-of-shift):
1) Stabilize bursty latency (P0)
   - action: temporary scale-up dedicated-gpu-pool-5 by +2 nodes (g5x2). cmd: kubectl -n inference scale deploy dedicated-pool-5 --replicas=8 (confirm autoscaler backoffs).
   - followup: open quick canary rule to route small customers to cheaper-variant (model-v1-8q) for 15m. JIRA-PLT-4312 created.
2) Rack A thermal ops (P1)
   - note: fans rattling on two nodes in A13 — schedule remote hands for A13-03 and A13-07. Tag hardware ticket: HW-TKT-1928.
3) KV cache GC/eviction anomaly (P1)
   - symptom: rare spike in generation cost for chat sessions when kv cache misses increment (seen 03/11 22:30). suspected stale prefix retention.
   - quick triage: check redis TTLs for prefix-cache: redis-prod-01:6379 keys: prefix:* ttl avg ~7200s but some >86400s which hints at orphaned keys. run: redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 --scan --pattern 'prefix:*' | xargs -L1 redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 ttl 

Small todos (sprint-y):
- [ ] Confirm canary routing policy doesn't break function-calls (test with function-calls-sim on dev).
- [ ] Add a temporary alert threshold for prefix-cache miss rate > 0.1% in the next hour.
- [ ] Notify Solutions Eng of potential degradation for customer ACME Corp (they're running long seq evals today). slack: @seng-acme
- [ ] Merge small runtime tweak (PR 987) if smoke tests pass (smoke: run on dedicated-pool-5, sequence len 1024, check p95).

Notes-to-self / diagnostics snippets:
- latency correlation: graph shows p50 increase correlates with 'batch_size' metric up -> suspected job batching misconfig. check batcher logs: kubectl logs batcher-*-pool5 | grep -i "batch_size" --last 200
- command to tail runtime logs across 3 pods: for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=runtime,pool=5 -o name); do kubectl logs -f $p --since=10m & done
- quick check on image versions: docker images on node: quay.redwood/runtime:stable-2026-02-28 vs pool-5 running stable-2026-02-14 -> possible mismatch. escalate if differences persist.

Capacity quick math (back-of-envelope):
- pool-5 current GPUs: 6xA100-80GB. avg tokens/s per GPU for model-x: ~640 tokens/s at 512 seq. expected throughput if +2 nodes: +1280 tokens/s -> should normalize p50.
- canary to cheaper-variant (8-bit quant): reduces tokens/s by ~10% latency but halves memory, useful for burst.

Thermal / hardware log:
- A12: temps nominal. A13: nodes 03/07 at 78C sustained. A14: one node auto-throttled, moved to spare pool. remote-hands asked to reseat mezz card and clean dust, approx ETA 4h.

Questions / followups for ops rotation handover:
- Did SRE push the fan firmware update last week? check HW-TKT-1889.
- Who approved autoscaler ramp yesterday? Need name for postmortem notes.

Random reminders (personal):
- Submit expense for conference travel (ID: EXP-558) before Friday.
- Lunch: try the new taqueria across mission st.

End-of-shift checklist:
- [ ] Confirm dedicated-pool-5 scaled back to normal after 30m stabilization window.
- [ ] Post summary to #platform-ops with links to JIRA and hardware tickets.
- [ ] Handoff: @Aaron Blake — follow up on disk SMART for node A14-02.

Timestamped quick add (03/12 11:40):
- merged PR 987, smoke passed on canary, latency improved to p50=48ms within 10m. keep open for 1h, then scale-down.

Misc scribbles:
- idea: add lightweight per-customer burst policy that auto-switches to quantized variant for <5m bursts. log metrics to 'burst_policy' stream.
- keep an eye on billing spike if rollouts happen in parallel.

-- Meera
